newsitem.title: USA: ABA VOTES TO CONDEMN CAMPAIGN FINANCE ABUSES.
newsitem.headline: ABA VOTES TO CONDEMN CAMPAIGN FINANCE ABUSES.

text.p: ABA delegates meeting in San Francisco on Wednesday adopted a resolution that condemns "pay-to-play" by lawyers that do business with elected government officials and calls for a task force to study the need for even tougher sanctions.
The problem is "acute," said Michael Cardozo, president of the Association of the Bar of the City of New York, which strongly urged the American Bar Association to take action on the issue.
"We should bring a halt to the practice," he said minutes before over 500 American Bar Association delegates approved the language.
Pay-to-play refers to bond professionals who give contributions to elected officials in return for bond business.
ABA delegates approved the two-page resolution after overwhelmingly rejecting a proposed amendment by one delegate calling for a study of whether the resolution abridges lawyers' free speech.
"It's unnecesary and ill advised," Jerome Shestack, ABA's new president, said about the rejected amendment. It "guts" the intent of the original plan, another lawyer said.
The following is the adopted resolution:
RESOLVED, that the American Bar Association:

1) condemns the conduct of lawyers making political campaign contributions to, and soliciting political campaign contributions for, public officials in return for being considered eligible by public agencies to perform professional services, including municipal finance arrangements;

2) calls on bar associations, lawyer disciplinary agencies and the judiciary to enforce, when applicable to prohibit this conduct, existing Rules of Professional Conduct, such as Model rule 7.2(c) prohibiting a lawyer from giving "anything of value to a person for recommending the lawyer's services";

3) condemns...public officials considering as eligible for engagement...only those lawyers who make political campaign contributions to, or solicit political campaign contribution for, public officials, and

4) calls upon legislative bodies, judicial rule-making agencies, bar associations, lawyer disciplinary agencies and public agencies to enact or adopt and enforce laws, rules and regulations that will discourage the conduct condemned in these resolutions.
FURTHER RESOLVED, that the House of Delegates requests the President of the American Bar Association to appoint a task force:

1) to review issues related to political campaign contributions made or solicited by lawyers and effective solutions thereto, including the "pay-to-play" rule proposed by The Association of the Bar of the City of New York in August 1997,

2) to determine whether additional professional standards, laws or procedures relating to political campaign contributions are necessary and desirable, including the conduct of lawyers making significant political campaign contributions to judicial candidates before whom the lawyers appear, and

3) to submit for consideration by the House of Delegates at its meeting in August 1998 recommendations as to any additional professional standards, laws or procedures found to be necessary and desirable in the form of amendments to the Model Rules of Professional Conduct, aspirational ethical standards, or other appropriate measures.
